column1: # Shared aontu unit tests. Columns (tab-separated): name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect
# mode: canon = unify(src).canon == expect ; gen = generate(src) deep-equals JSON(expect) ; err = generate(src) errors, message contains expect
# Escapes in src/expect: \n -> newline, \t -> tab, \\ -> backslash. Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# FLIPPED by the number tower's D7 (docs/design/number-tower.md): an
# integer-source literal that binary64 cannot hold EXACTLY is a located
# error instead of a silently rounded value. 0xffffffffffffffff is
# 2^64-1, which rounds up to 2^64, so `hex-big` and `hex-big-canon` --
# which pinned that rounded value, 18446744073709552000, in gen and in
# canon -- become one err row. The refusal's hint names the `0d` escape;
# number-tower.tsv pins the hint text and the escape itself.
# THE RULE IS EXACTNESS, NOT MAGNITUDE, and hex-huge is the row that
# says so: 0x10...0 is 2^124, a power of two, therefore exactly
# representable, therefore still a value -- at a magnitude eighteen
# orders of ten LARGER than the literal above it that is refused.
# UTF-16 SURROGATE PAIRS IN QUOTED STRINGS
# An astral character has several spellings and all of them must denote
# the same value. Three of these used to be Go-only failures: the pair
# lookahead in @tabnas/parser's Go lexer lived inside the 4-hex escape
# branch and recognised only its own spelling, while the braced branch
# had no lookahead at all -- so a braced half, or either mixed pair,
# decoded to two U+FFFD and Go REJECTED documents TypeScript accepted
# (issue #24). Fixed upstream in parser 0.8.4 by pairing on the decoded
# code unit sequence, so the spelling of each half no longer matters.
# In this file a cell's \\ becomes one backslash, so `\\u{d83d}` reaches
# the engine as the seven characters \u{d83d}.
# Escaped and literal spellings must UNIFY -- the value, not the source,
# is what unification sees. This pair errored in Go before the fix.
# In every position, not just a bare value.
# Bare/unquoted text processes no escapes -- and, since 0.58.0, cannot
# hold a backslash at all: the bare-text rule refuses it (op-chars.tsv),
# so the lone-surrogate question never arises outside a string. This
# agreed across ports throughout and must keep agreeing -- a fix inside
# the string matcher that reaches here has overreached.
# SRC passes through the runner's unescape only, so `\\ud800` is the six
